top_concerns: Over‑estimation of low‑yield diagnoses (NSAID nephrotoxicity, DI‑IN, rare hemoglobinopathies)
Under‑estimation of CKD‑related anemia and CKD‑MBD prevalence
Failure to include acute kidney injury as a separate consideration despite critical lab flag
Unconfirmed diabetes status undermines ranking of diabetic nephropathy
Missing secondary hypertension work‑up (renin, aldosterone, imaging)
review_summary: The differential is comprehensive but mis‑weights several low‑probability entities and omits an acute‑on‑chronic kidney injury component. Evidence strongly supports hypertensive nephrosclerosis as the primary etiology, while anemia of chronic disease and CKD‑MBD are under‑represented. Clarification of diabetes status, repeat creatinine, quantitative proteinuria, and targeted secondary‑hypertension testing are essential to refine probabilities.
